title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. These notes compute the outer action of Gal(Qbar/Q), or more generally of automorphisms u of a profinite fundamental groupoid, on pi_1 of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity} (Grothendieck's Pi_{0,3}). The groupoid uses a set of base points stable under the symmetry group G_J = S_3 x {1,tau}, where tau is complex conjugation.

The picture. The figure shows the Riemann sphere with:
- the three punctures 0, 1, infinity (black dots) on the real equator;
- three base points Q_0, Q_1, Q_infinity, one on each real interval between punctures;
- two poles P^+ and P^-. These are the points e^{±i pi/3}, the two fixed points of the order-3 rotation rho, which tau exchanges.
- Arcs ã_i^± run in the upper/lower hemisphere from Q_i to Q_{omega i}, where omega is the cyclic orientation attached to the hemisphere.
- Arcs d_i^± run from the pole P^± to Q_i.
The set underline-omega = {+,-} of the two cyclic orientations indexes the two hemispheres.

Groupoid III_J -> IV_J. Groupoid III_J (previous pages) has vertices Q_i, arcs ã_i^omega and the 'trivial cocycle' relations (16). Here Grothendieck adds the two vertices P^omega and the arcs d_i^omega, with tau(P^omega) = P^{omega'} and tau(d_i^omega) = d_i^{omega'}. He imposes the six triangle relations (35): (d_{omega i}^omega)^{-1} ã_i^omega d_i^omega = 1. Each triangle P^omega, Q_i, Q_{omega i} contains no puncture, so the relation holds. The resulting groupoid IV_J is equivalent to III_J, and the triangle relations imply the hexagon (cocycle) relations of III_J.

The automorphisms u. Next he considers automorphisms u of IV_J that fix the vertices and commute with G_J. By G_J-equivariance (S_3 transitive on the Q_i and on the d's of one hemisphere, tau swapping hemispheres), such a u is determined by two elements of the completed group Pi_{0,3}, each transported to every arc by the symmetry isomorphisms psi:
- one element alpha for all the ã's;
- one element xi for all the d's.
The margin note says xi is unconstrained. The triangle relation (35) then forces (37): alpha = xi · rho^{-1}(xi^{-1}).

Why this matters. The previous page showed alpha must lie in V = {x : x rho^{-1}(x) rho^{-2}(x) = 1}; this is the 3-cycle (pentagon-free, 'hexagon') relation of GT-type. Formula (37) solves that relation automatically as a 'coboundary': alpha rho^{-1}(alpha) rho^{-2}(alpha) = xi rho^{-3}(xi)^{-1} = 1 because rho^3 = 1. The 3-cycle relation thus becomes a triviality once one passes through the rho-fixed base point P^+.

Next page. The tau-compatibility gives beta = xi sigma_inf(xi)^{-1} with beta sigma_inf(beta) = 1, i.e. the 2-cycle relation.

Top-left NB. The arrows ã_i^omega are not in fact (tau-)symmetric, cf. (37) and the comment on p. 19. This is consistent with alpha being a coboundary of xi.

Overall. The page is part of Grothendieck's hands-on derivation of the defining relations of what became the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group: the 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations for the Galois action on Pi_{0,3}. The method is the 'Lego' with symmetric base points (midpoints of real intervals and the points e^{±i pi/3}).
errors: Simplification declared by Grothendieck himself: he only treats u fixing all vertices. Galois elements not fixing Q(sqrt(-3)) exchange P^+ and P^-, so the genuine Galois case needs the vertex-permuting automorphisms he says 'il faudra regarder'.

Indexing/convention ambiguities: psi_{omega i}^omega versus psi_i^omega, and rho versus rho^{-1} in (37). The next page itself queries 'rho^{-1}?' in (39). The structural conclusion (alpha is a rho-coboundary of a free xi, hence satisfies the 3-cycle relation) holds under either convention.

ideas.what: Groupoid on the symmetric base points (midpoints Q_i of real intervals and the two rho-fixed points P^±), with triangle relations; equivalence III_J ≃ IV_J
ideas.modern_name: Lego / fundamental groupoid with tangential or symmetric base points of M_{0,4}; two-dimensional cell decomposition of M_{0,4}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984); developed by Ihara, Drinfeld, Lochak–Schneps, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (qualitative description of the Teichmüller Lego and its symmetric base points)

ideas.what: Parametrization of G_J-equivariant automorphisms by a free element xi, with alpha = xi rho^{-1}(xi)^{-1}, making the 3-cycle relation automatic
ideas.modern_name: 3-cycle (hexagon-type) relation of GT, f(x,y) = ... solved via the base point e^{i pi/3}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990) and Ihara (1990-91) for the GT relations; the use of the base point e^{i pi/3} appears in Ihara and Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Not explicitly; Esquisse only alludes to the relations coming from M_{0,4} and M_{0,5}

missed.claim: This is an explicit, pre-Drinfeld derivation of the GT 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations. It works with an automorphism of the symmetric-base-point groupoid commuting with S_3 x {complex conjugation}. The 3-cycle relation appears as the cocycle condition of the 'xi-coboundary' through the rho-fixed point.
missed.quote: il n'y a pas de condition sur ξ ... (37) α̃ = ξ·ρ^{-1}(ξ^{-1}) , i.e. α̃ est connu quand on connaît ξ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck had the concrete defining relations (in coboundary form) years before Drinfeld/Ihara, beyond the qualitative claims in the Esquisse. Historically relevant to the attribution of GT; mathematically known.

missed.claim: He defers the case of automorphisms that permute the vertices P^± or the Q_i, which is exactly what is needed for elements of Gal(Qbar/Q) outside Gal(Qbar/Q(sqrt(-3))).
missed.quote: il faudra regarder aussi ceux qui permutent les sommets P_ω, ou les Q_i
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor; the modern treatment with the vertex-swapping case is standard (Ihara, Lochak–Schneps).

deep.surprise_reason: A nice explicit precursor of the GT relations, using the e^{±iπ/3} base points and a coboundary trick. However, Grothendieck's anticipation of GT via the M_{0,4} Lego is well known, and these manuscripts have been studied (e.g. by Schneps). The relations themselves are standard.
transcription_corrections: In the figure and line (11) the added vertices are the two poles P^+ and P^- (P^ω, ω ∈ {+,-}). 'P_∞^ω' is likely a misreading of P^ω or P_ω.
(35) is likely (d^ω_{ωi})^{-1} ã^ω_i d^ω_i = 1, a triangle relation with ã_i^ω : Q_i → Q_{ωi}.
Top-left NB probably reads 'ne sont pas en fait invariantes/symétriques' (referring to τ-symmetry), cf. (37) and commentaire p. 19.
